title: Finite normalization of a generically smooth curve over a separably closed valuation base
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-weil-field, def-kun-separably-closed] and $V\subseteq K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ belongs to $V$. Assume the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], flat and finitely presented over $T$ [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with all nonempty fibres pure of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and with smooth generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Pure dimension one means that every irreducible component has dimension one. Then the normalization $n:X^\nu\to X$ in its function field [def-sc-normalization] is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], is an isomorphism on the generic fibre, and $X^\nu$ is normal, flat and finitely presented over $T$ with all nonempty fibres pure of dimension one. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].

source.place: Section 4.1, opening paragraph, printed p. 25: finiteness and finite presentation of normalization from Theorem 3.5.5 and Proposition 3.5.2; smooth-generic-fibre case of this normalization assertion. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.
